_comment: CANONICAL authored brochure copy for curaos.abualruz.com. PUBLIC product brochure (no PHI, no tenant data). This workspace mirror is the canonical authoring source per the repo-boundary rule; scripts/build.sh on the box resolves --content-dir to the repo copy (content/site.json), which is kept byte-synced with this file. examples/site-content/site.json is a MINIMAL build/test fixture only. Every claim is verified against the CuraOS charter (AGENTS.md) and what is actually live: 19 frontend apps + around 60 backend services reachable on *.abualruz.com, API at api.abualruz.com, Pocket-ID OIDC brokered by identity-service, dark mode + RTL/Arabic working. Capability claims that are not yet GA are framed as design intent. Zero em-dashes or en-dashes (binding rule). App and demo hrefs are literal https URLs (the live hosts); docs/releases/demo use {docsUrl}/{releasesUrl}/{demoUrl} tokens resolved from the same build flags as the hero CTAs.
headline: The care platform you actually own
subhead: A generic neutral core with opt-in Health, Education, and ERP overlays. Nineteen apps and around sixty backend services run right now, self-hosted on Kubernetes, composed from one codebase and one shared design system.
positioning: Self-hosted first. Event-led. Multi-tenant from one codebase. No managed-cloud lock-in.
description: CuraOS is a composable, self-hosted-first platform: a generic neutral core with opt-in vertical overlays (Health, Education, ERP). It runs today as 19 frontend apps on a shared design system and around 60 backend services on self-hosted Kubernetes, with single sign-on through Pocket-ID, and is designed to deploy across cloud, on-prem, hybrid, and air-gapped targets. CuraOS is in active development (pre-1.0); the deployment profiles and overlay depth harden along the roadmap.

pillars.title: Self-hosted first
pillars.blurb: Designed to run on your own infrastructure with no managed-cloud lock-in. Cloud, on-prem, hybrid, and air-gapped are first-class targets, not afterthoughts.

pillars.title: Generic before vertical
pillars.blurb: The neutral core comes first and stays reusable. Vertical overlays extend it through documented seams; they never fork it.

pillars.title: Event-led
pillars.blurb: Durable, versioned event contracts are the primary integration path, with sync APIs second. Services stay loosely coupled by design.

pillars.title: Multi-tenant
pillars.blurb: Built so SaaS, on-prem, and hybrid all run from one codebase, with tenant data isolation as a core boundary (PHI and PII stay in overlay schemas).

pillars.title: Builder-led
pillars.blurb: Experiences are composed through a workflow/BPM engine and an app/site builder, so behavior is configured against documented seams rather than hand-forked.

pillars.title: Composable
pillars.blurb: Services, libraries, and clients ship independently and combine per tenant and per market. Take only the pieces you need.

apps.caption: Nineteen apps, live now
apps.intro: Every app is generated from the same workflow definitions and domain contracts, themed by one shared design system, and reachable today on its own subdomain. Sign-in is OIDC through Pocket-ID, brokered by the identity service into a CuraOS session. Dark mode and right-to-left Arabic are built in and persist across reloads.

capabilities.caption: The platform underneath
capabilities.intro: Every app sits on the same foundation. The neutral core provides reusable capabilities; vertical overlays extend it. Behavior is built, not forked. A first set of services already serves real data through live read endpoints, while the rest are scaffolded and filling in along the roadmap.

items.title: Workflow and BPM core
items.blurb: Orchestrates human tasks, automation, and SLA timing. Every domain routes through it, so process logic lives in one place.

items.title: App and site builder
items.blurb: Generates admin, ops, and external surfaces from BPM definitions, domain contracts, and shared theming.

items.title: Automation core
items.blurb: Low-code actions, connectors, and scheduling so integrations and routine work are configured rather than coded.

items.title: Neutral capabilities
items.blurb: Identity, tenancy, party, audit, notify, search, reports, storage, calendar, tasks, documents, commerce, and more, all vertical-agnostic.

items.title: Vertical overlays
items.blurb: HealthStack (patient, encounter, clinical, consent, interop) plus Education and ERP, extending the core through documented seams.

items.title: Versioned contracts
items.blurb: APIs and durable events carry versioned schemas with deprecation windows, so services evolve without breaking consumers.

architecture.caption: Opt-in vertical overlays sit on top of one neutral core and depend downward on it. The dependency direction is always toward the core, never the reverse. The system runs as composable services on Kubernetes with CNPG Postgres, Valkey, and event-led messaging; the public edge is fronted by Caddy and Cloudflare.

deployProfiles.name: Cloud SaaS
deployProfiles.blurb: Target profile: vendor-managed, per-tenant isolation, horizontal scale.

deployProfiles.name: On-prem
deployProfiles.blurb: Running profile: single tenant on self-hosted Kubernetes with overlays opt-in. This is how the live deployment runs today.

deployProfiles.name: Hybrid
deployProfiles.blurb: Target profile: vendor control plane with your data plane, so audit and secrets stay on your infrastructure.

deployProfiles.name: Home lab / air-gap
deployProfiles.blurb: Target profile: single tenant, fully offline, designed for zero external calls. Zero-egress is proven for the platform's own infrastructure and this site, not yet for a full product tenant.

status.caption: What is shipped, and what is next
status.intro: CuraOS is pre-1.0. We would rather you know the boundary than discover it. Here is the honest line between what runs today and what is still on the roadmap.

columns.heading: Shipped today
items: 19 frontend apps generated from one design system and shared contracts, with dark mode and RTL Arabic
Around 60 backend services deployed on self-hosted Kubernetes
A first set of services (commerce, orders, fleet, calendar, donation, site, automation, plugin-runtime) serving real seeded data through live read endpoints
OIDC sign-in (Authorization Code with PKCE) through Pocket-ID, brokered by the identity service
Workflow/BPM core, app/site builder, and automation core
Versioned API and durable event contracts with deprecation windows
Air-gap zero-egress proven for the platform's own infrastructure and this site

columns.heading: On the roadmap
items: Full domain depth inside each service (scaffold to feature-complete)
A shipped curaos CLI for tenant composition (the quickstart is illustrative)
A public, self-serve multi-tenant demo tenant
GA hardening of the cloud, hybrid, and air-gap deployment profiles
Air-gap zero-egress proven end to end for a full product tenant
Education and ERP overlays brought to parity with HealthStack
